'''Brian Poindexter''' (born August 4, 1979) is an American politician who is the member-elect to the [[United States House of Representatives]] for {{ushr|OH|7}}. A member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]], he has served as a city councilmember in [[Brook Park, Ohio|Brook Park]] since 2018.

==Early life and career==
Poindexter was born on August 4, 1979, in [[Cleveland]], [[Ohio]].<ref name=nytimes>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/08/us/politics/brian-poindexter-max-miller-ohio-house.html|title=Amid Abuse Claims Against Max Miller, This Democrat Thinks He Can Win His Seat|first=Emily|last=Davies|date=August 8, 2026|work=The New York Times|accessdate=August 9, 2026}}</ref><ref name=guardian>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/apr/18/brian-poindexter-ohio-congress-candidate|title=An iron worker takes on one of Trump’s most loyal followers in Congress|first=Michael|last=Sainato|date=April 18, 2026|work=The Guardian|accessdate=August 9, 2026}}</ref> His father Bob was a union [[machinist]], while his mother [[stay-at-home mother|stayed at home]].<ref name=nytimes /><ref name=guardian /> He has five siblings.<ref name=nytimes /> His grandfather was an [[Automotive industry|autoworker]].<ref name=guardian /> In high school, Poindexter played on the school [[American football|football]], [[baseball]] and [[wrestling]] teams as well as working at a [[machine shop]].<ref name="WorkingClassStory">{{cite web |last1=Poindexter |first1=Brian |title=Brian's Working-Class Story |url=https://poindexterforcongress.com/brian-poindexters-working-class-story/ |publisher=Brian Poindexter for Congress |access-date=November 4, 2026 |date=2026}}</ref> During his teenage years, Poindexter accrued several [[misdemeanor]] charges for [[public intoxication]], speeding and [[assault]], the latter of which being the result of an incident where Poindexter and his friends had a fight with "some other dudes" at a beach in Cleveland.<ref name=nytimes />

After graduating high school, Poindexter obtained a Class A [[commercial driver's license]] and began working in the [[moving industry]], where he travelled across the whole of the [[continental United States]].<ref name="WorkingClassStory" /><ref name="WFPEndorse26">{{cite web |title=WFP Endorses Brian Poindexter in OH-07 |url=https://workingfamilies.org/2026/04/wfp-endorses-brian-poindexter-for-oh-07/ |publisher=[[Working Families Party]] |access-date=November 4, 2026 |date=April 20, 2026}}</ref> In 2007, he joined the [[International Association of Bridge, Structural, Ornamental and Reinforcing Iron Workers]] and began an [[apprenticeship]] in ironworking while completing an [[associate degree]] in applied industrial technology at [[Cuyahoga Community College]].<ref name="WorkingClassStory" /><ref name="WFPEndorse26" />

From 2012 to 2014, Poindexter served as a [[union organizer]].<ref name="WorkingClassStory" /><ref name="WFPEndorse26" /> In 2014, he re-entered the workforce as an ironworker and worked on several projects over the next few years including [[The Lumen]] and [[NASA Glenn Research Center]].<ref name="WorkingClassStory" /><ref name="WFPEndorse26" /> He was an apprentice instructor at Ironworks Local 17 until May 2026.<ref name="SpectrumNews">{{cite web |last1=Leigh |first1=Harri |title=Brian Poindexter's balancing act in race reshaped by Max Miller scandal |url=https://spectrumnews1.com/oh/columbus/news/2026/09/02/brian-poindexter-max-miller- |publisher=[[Spectrum News#Spectrum News 1 (Ohio)|Spectrum News 1]] |access-date=November 4, 2026 |date=September 4, 2026}}</ref>

Poindexter was elected to the at-large district of the [[city council]] of [[Brook Park, Ohio]] in 2017 and he began his term in January 2018.<ref name=guardian /> He was re-elected for five terms and his final term will end in January 2027.<ref name=guardian />

==U.S. House of Representatives==
In January 2026, Poindexter announced his candidacy for the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] nomination for the [[U.S. House of Representatives]] for {{ushr|OH|7}}.<ref>{{cite web|last=Zurick|first=Maura|title=From Brook Park City Hall to Capitol Hill: Brian Poindexter outlines vision for congressional race|work=Cleveland Plain-Dealer|date=January 27, 2026|url=https://www.cleveland.com/news/2026/01/from-brook-park-city-hall-to-capitol-hill-brian-poindexter-outlines-vision-in-congressional-race.html|access-date=August 9, 2026}}</ref> He won the nomination in the primary election in May with 37% of the vote, while second-place finisher [[Ed FitzGerald]], former [[County Executive of Cuyahoga County, Ohio|Cuyahoga county executive]], earned 22%.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cleveland.com/election/2026/05/brian-poindexter-wins-ohios-7th-district-dem-primary-incumbents-joyce-brown-fend-off-challengers.html|title=Brian Poindexter wins Ohio’s 7th District Dem primary, incumbents Joyce, Brown fend off challengers|first=Sabrina|last=Eaton|date=May 6, 2026|work=Cleveland Plain-Dealer|accessdate=August 9, 2026}}</ref> Poindexter defeated [[Max Miller (politician)|Max Miller]] in the November general election.<ref name="Results">{{cite web |last1=Eaton |first1=Sabrina |title=Brian Poindexter flips Trump-leaning Ohio district, ousting U.S. Rep. Max Miller |url=https://www.cleveland.com/news/2026/11/brian-poindexter-flips-trump-leaning-ohio-district-ousting-us-rep-max-miller.html |publisher=[[The Plain Dealer|cleveland.com]] |access-date=November 4, 2026 |date=November 4, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Poindexter and his now ex-wife have three daughters together.<ref name=nytimes/><ref>{{cite web |last1=Zimmermann |first1=David |title=Max Miller’s Democratic opponent spotlights daughters in campaign ad |url=https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/campaigns/congressional/4707522/max-miller-brian-poindexter-daughter-campaign-ad/ |publisher=[[Washington Examiner]] |access-date=November 4, 2026 |date=September 1, 2026}}</ref> He is a fan of the [[Cleveland Browns]] and was once arrested at a Browns game for fighting with a [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] fan.<ref name=nytimes/>
